rv.q: Elyot provides a snapshot of men at a crunch-point.
This bittersweet 1980s comedy offers a frank, moving portrait of gay relationships just before the Aids crisis.
Under Adam Spreadbury-Maher's direction, the acting and dialogue are naturalistic, the sexual scenes and descriptions frank — even full-frontal.
This lends an unnecessarily oppressive air to a play that’s actually all about liberation and making choices.
The story unfolds without any surprises.
This play may be a tad dated, but I found it involving throughout, even if the denouement is rather obvious and its two hour length just right.
For that reason, and for four quality performances, Elyot's debut is well worth a look.
London is lucky to have a third opportunity to see this fascinating and emotional play which has been staged beautifully.
